newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's VAW defends EU aluminium import tariff.
newsitem.headline: Germany's VAW defends EU aluminium import tariff.

text.p: The European Union's six percent import tariff on aluminium should be retained, a spokesman for Germany's VAW aluminium AG said on Monday.
"Together with the majority of European producers, we support a continuation of the tariff," he said in response to an enquiry by Reuters.
"This position was put forward during the last GATT round of world trade talks and accepted by the EU Commission, there is no need to revise it."
VAW, part of utility group Viag AG, accounted for 416,000 tonnes of Germany's total aluminium production of 575,155 tonnes last year.
The figure included production at overseas shareholdings.
EU aluminium processors and hopeful third country suppliers have called for the elimination of the tariff which they say distorts trade and penalises fabricators with higher costs.
They may bring it up at a World Trade Organisation meeting in Singapore in December.

The EU is the only trading bloc applying a duty on imports of unwrought aluminium, because of higher costs, it says. But it offers preferential terms to certain LOME and EFTA countries. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
